vulnerabilities.title: Application is debuggable
vulnerabilities.details: android:debuggable="true" lets anyone with USB/ADB access attach a debugger (JDWP), dump memory, bypass checks at runtime and read the private data directory via `run-as`. Release builds must never ship with this flag.
vulnerabilities.description: android:debuggable="true" lets anyone with USB/ADB access attach a debugger (JDWP), dump memory, bypass checks at runtime and read the private data directory via `run-as`. Release builds must never ship with this flag.

vulnerabilities.title: Cleartext HTTP traffic allowed
vulnerabilities.details: android:usesCleartextTraffic="true" allows unencrypted HTTP connections to any host. Anyone on the same Wi-Fi / network path can read and modify traffic (credentials, session tokens, API responses).
vulnerabilities.description: android:usesCleartextTraffic="true" allows unencrypted HTTP connections to any host. Anyone on the same Wi-Fi / network path can read and modify traffic (credentials, session tokens, API responses).
vulnerabilities.remediation: Set usesCleartextTraffic="false" and serve every endpoint over HTTPS. If a legacy host needs HTTP, scope it with a network_security_config domain-config.

vulnerabilities.title: Exported content providers without effective protection
vulnerabilities.type: Exported content providers without effective protection
vulnerabilities.details: 1 provider(s) can be invoked by any app on the device. Other apps can query/insert/update/delete through these providers. Unprotected providers commonly lead to data leaks, SQL injection in selection arguments and path traversal via openFile().
vulnerabilities.description: 1 provider(s) can be invoked by any app on the device. Other apps can query/insert/update/delete through these providers. Unprotected providers commonly lead to data leaks, SQL injection in selection arguments and path traversal via openFile().
vulnerabilities.remediation:
Set android:exported="false" unless other apps must use the provider. If they must, guard it with a signature-level permission and use parameterized queries:

<permission android:name="com.example.permission.DATA"
            android:protectionLevel="signature"/>
<provider android:name=".DataProvider"
          android:exported="true"
          android:readPermission="com.example.permission.DATA"
          android:writePermission="com.example.permission.DATA"/>

vulnerabilities.title: Signed with the Android debug certificate
vulnerabilities.type: Signed with the Android debug certificate
vulnerabilities.details: The APK is signed with an auto-generated debug keystore (CN=Android Debug). Debug builds are not meant for distribution: the key is unprotected on developer machines, and debug builds usually carry debug flags and endpoints.
vulnerabilities.description: The APK is signed with an auto-generated debug keystore (CN=Android Debug). Debug builds are not meant for distribution: the key is unprotected on developer machines, and debug builds usually carry debug flags and endpoints.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Sign releases with a dedicated, protected upload key (Play App Signing).

vulnerabilities.title: WebView allows universal access from file URLs
vulnerabilities.type: WebView allows universal access from file URLs
vulnerabilities.details: setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs(true) lets JavaScript in a file:// page read ANY origin and local file, so a single malicious HTML file can exfiltrate app data.
vulnerabilities.description: setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs(true) lets JavaScript in a file:// page read ANY origin and local file, so a single malicious HTML file can exfiltrate app data.
vulnerabilities.remediation:
Pass false (the secure default on modern API levels):

webView.getSettings().setAllowUniversalAccessFromFileURLs(false);

vulnerabilities.title: WebView ignores TLS certificate errors
vulnerabilities.details: WebViewClient.onReceivedSslError() calls handler.proceed(), so invalid, self-signed or attacker certificates are silently accepted and HTTPS pages can be intercepted.
vulnerabilities.description: WebViewClient.onReceivedSslError() calls handler.proceed(), so invalid, self-signed or attacker certificates are silently accepted and HTTPS pages can be intercepted.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Call handler.cancel() (the default) and fix the server certificate instead.

vulnerabilities.title: Overly broad FileProvider paths
vulnerabilities.details: FileProvider androidx.core.content.FileProvider (res/xml/provider_paths.xml) can grant access to far more files than needed. If any code path builds a content URI from user input (e.g. a share/export feature) attackers can read private files such as databases and shared_prefs.
vulnerabilities.description: FileProvider androidx.core.content.FileProvider (res/xml/provider_paths.xml) can grant access to far more files than needed. If any code path builds a content URI from user input (e.g. a share/export feature) attackers can read private files such as databases and shared_prefs.
vulnerabilities.remediation:
Share only dedicated sub-directories:

<paths>
    <files-path name="shared" path="shared/"/>
</paths>

vulnerabilities.title: Possible intent redirection from exported component
vulnerabilities.type: Possible intent redirection from exported component
vulnerabilities.details: Exported components read a nested Intent from extras (getParcelableExtra / Intent.parseUri) and launch it. A malicious app can make them start private, non-exported components or grant URI permissions to private files.
vulnerabilities.description: Exported components read a nested Intent from extras (getParcelableExtra / Intent.parseUri) and launch it. A malicious app can make them start private, non-exported components or grant URI permissions to private files.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Never launch intents received from extras. If needed, validate the target with intent.resolveActivity() against an allow-list and strip FLAG_GRANT_* flags.

vulnerabilities.title: Untrusted Intent / deep-link data loaded into WebView
vulnerabilities.type: Untrusted Intent / deep-link data loaded into WebView
vulnerabilities.details: Exported (or deep-link) activities read URLs from the incoming Intent and pass data to WebView.loadUrl(). Attackers can open arbitrary pages inside the app (phishing, XSS against the JavaScript bridge, file:// theft).
vulnerabilities.description: Exported (or deep-link) activities read URLs from the incoming Intent and pass data to WebView.loadUrl(). Attackers can open arbitrary pages inside the app (phishing, XSS against the JavaScript bridge, file:// theft).
vulnerabilities.remediation: Parse the URI and accept only https URLs whose host is on a strict allow-list before loading.

vulnerabilities.title: Application data backup enabled
vulnerabilities.details: android:allowBackup is true. Application data (SharedPreferences, databases, files) can be extracted with `adb backup` and is included in cloud/device-to-device transfers, exposing session tokens and PII.
vulnerabilities.description: android:allowBackup is true. Application data (SharedPreferences, databases, files) can be extracted with `adb backup` and is included in cloud/device-to-device transfers, exposing session tokens and PII.
vulnerabilities.remediation:
Disable backups or exclude sensitive files explicitly:

<application android:allowBackup="false"
             android:dataExtractionRules="@xml/data_extraction_rules"
             android:fullBackupContent="@xml/backup_rules">

vulnerabilities.title: Custom permission with weak protectionLevel
vulnerabilities.details: These custom permissions use protectionLevel normal/dangerous, so any app can simply request them and gain access to the components they 'protect'.
vulnerabilities.description: These custom permissions use protectionLevel normal/dangerous, so any app can simply request them and gain access to the components they 'protect'.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use android:protectionLevel="signature" for permissions that guard internal components.

vulnerabilities.title: Exported activities without protection
vulnerabilities.details: 5 activity(s) can be invoked by any app on the device. Any installed app can launch these screens directly, skipping login flows and passing crafted extras (intent spoofing, UI/auth bypass, data injection).
vulnerabilities.description: 5 activity(s) can be invoked by any app on the device. Any installed app can launch these screens directly, skipping login flows and passing crafted extras (intent spoofing, UI/auth bypass, data injection).
vulnerabilities.evidence:
com.insecureshop.ChooserActivity  —  implicit (has intent-filter)
com.insecureshop.AboutUsActivity  —  android:exported="true"
com.insecureshop.WebViewActivity  —  implicit (has intent-filter)
com.insecureshop.WebView2Activity  —  implicit (has intent-filter)
com.insecureshop.ResultActivity  —  android:exported="true"
vulnerabilities.remediation:
Set android:exported="false" on components that are only used internally. For components that must be reachable, require a signature-level permission and validate every extra:

<activity android:name=".Foo"
    android:exported="true"
    android:permission="com.example.permission.INTERNAL"/>

<permission android:name="com.example.permission.INTERNAL"
            android:protectionLevel="signature"/>

vulnerabilities.title: Short RSA signing key
vulnerabilities.details: The signing key is RSA-1024, below the 2048-bit minimum.
vulnerabilities.description: The signing key is RSA-1024, below the 2048-bit minimum.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Rotate to an RSA-4096 or EC P-256 key using APK Signature Scheme v3.

vulnerabilities.title: Custom URL scheme deep links
vulnerabilities.details: Custom schemes can be registered by any app, so links may be hijacked, and every parameter arrives from untrusted web content. Validate all deep-link input before using it (especially URLs passed to WebViews or intents).
vulnerabilities.description: Custom schemes can be registered by any app, so links may be hijacked, and every parameter arrives from untrusted web content. Validate all deep-link input before using it (especially URLs passed to WebViews or intents).
vulnerabilities.remediation: Prefer verified Android App Links (https + autoVerify) and strictly validate host, path and query parameters in the handling activity.

vulnerabilities.title: JavaScript enabled in WebView
vulnerabilities.details: WebSettings.setJavaScriptEnabled(true) is called. If the WebView renders any content an attacker can influence (deep-link URLs, HTTP pages, user data) this enables XSS inside the app context.
vulnerabilities.description: WebSettings.setJavaScriptEnabled(true) is called. If the WebView renders any content an attacker can influence (deep-link URLs, HTTP pages, user data) this enables XSS inside the app context.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Enable JavaScript only for trusted, HTTPS-loaded content and validate every URL before loadUrl().

vulnerabilities.title: Supports obsolete Android versions
vulnerabilities.details: minSdkVersion is 16. Android versions below 5.0 lack modern TLS defaults, WebView updates, and are vulnerable to well-known platform bugs (e.g. addJavascriptInterface RCE, Janus, FakeID).
vulnerabilities.description: minSdkVersion is 16. Android versions below 5.0 lack modern TLS defaults, WebView updates, and are vulnerable to well-known platform bugs (e.g. addJavascriptInterface RCE, Janus, FakeID).
vulnerabilities.remediation: Raise minSdkVersion to at least 23 (Android 6.0).

vulnerabilities.title: Targets an outdated API level
vulnerabilities.details: targetSdkVersion is 29. The app opts out of newer platform protections (explicit exported flags, PendingIntent mutability, package visibility, scoped storage) and cannot be published on Google Play.
vulnerabilities.description: targetSdkVersion is 29. The app opts out of newer platform protections (explicit exported flags, PendingIntent mutability, package visibility, scoped storage) and cannot be published on Google Play.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Raise targetSdkVersion to the current Play requirement and adapt to the behaviour changes.

vulnerabilities.title: Weak certificate signature algorithm
vulnerabilities.details: The signing certificate uses SHA1withRSA. This mainly matters for the v1 (JAR) scheme, where digests of SHA-1 are accepted by old devices.
vulnerabilities.description: The signing certificate uses SHA1withRSA. This mainly matters for the v1 (JAR) scheme, where digests of SHA-1 are accepted by old devices.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use a SHA-256 based key/certificate for new apps (key rotation via v3 for existing ones).

vulnerabilities.title: Data written to shared external storage
vulnerabilities.type: Data written to shared external storage
vulnerabilities.details: The app uses public external storage. Files there are readable by other apps with storage permissions and survive uninstall - never store tokens, PII or downloaded code there.
vulnerabilities.description: The app uses public external storage. Files there are readable by other apps with storage permissions and survive uninstall - never store tokens, PII or downloaded code there.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use Context.getFilesDir() / getCacheDir() for private data, or EncryptedFile for sensitive files.

vulnerabilities.title: Hardcoded cleartext HTTP endpoints
vulnerabilities.details: 1 http:// URL(s) are embedded. If any of them is contacted at runtime, the traffic and responses can be read or modified by a network attacker.
vulnerabilities.description: 1 http:// URL(s) are embedded. If any of them is contacted at runtime, the traffic and responses can be read or modified by a network attacker.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Switch every endpoint to HTTPS and block cleartext in network_security_config.

vulnerabilities.title: Janus exposure on Android 5.0-6.0 devices
vulnerabilities.details: Devices below Android 7.0 only verify the v1 signature, which is susceptible to the Janus attack (CVE-2017-13156) on unpatched 5.x/6.x devices.
vulnerabilities.description: Devices below Android 7.0 only verify the v1 signature, which is susceptible to the Janus attack (CVE-2017-13156) on unpatched 5.x/6.x devices.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Raise minSdkVersion to 24+ so only v2+ verification is used.

vulnerabilities.title: Sensitive screens can be captured (no FLAG_SECURE)
vulnerabilities.type: Sensitive screens can be captured (no FLAG_SECURE)
vulnerabilities.details: No use of WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_SECURE was found. Login/payment screens appear in the recents thumbnail, screenshots and screen recordings (and to screen-capturing malware).
vulnerabilities.description: No use of WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_SECURE was found. Login/payment screens appear in the recents thumbnail, screenshots and screen recordings (and to screen-capturing malware).
vulnerabilities.remediation: getWindow().setFlags(WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_SECURE, WindowManager.LayoutParams.FLAG_SECURE);

vulnerabilities.title: Tapjacking on sensitive screens
vulnerabilities.details: targetSdkVersion 29 < 31 and these sensitive-looking screens do not filter touches when obscured, so an overlay can trick users into tapping.
vulnerabilities.description: targetSdkVersion 29 < 31 and these sensitive-looking screens do not filter touches when obscured, so an overlay can trick users into tapping.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Set android:filterTouchesWhenObscured="true" on sensitive views/activities and target API 31+.

vulnerabilities.title: Exported services without protection
vulnerabilities.details: 1 service(s) can be invoked by any app on the device. Any app can start or bind to these services and invoke their functionality with attacker-controlled input. All of them belong to third-party SDKs.
vulnerabilities.description: 1 service(s) can be invoked by any app on the device. Any app can start or bind to these services and invoke their functionality with attacker-controlled input. All of them belong to third-party SDKs.
vulnerabilities.remediation:
Set android:exported="false" on components that are only used internally. For components that must be reachable, require a signature-level permission and validate every extra:

<service android:name=".Foo"
    android:exported="true"
    android:permission="com.example.permission.INTERNAL"/>

<permission android:name="com.example.permission.INTERNAL"
            android:protectionLevel="signature"/>

vulnerabilities.title: No root / integrity detection
vulnerabilities.details: No root detection, Play Integrity or SafetyNet attestation was found. For apps handling money or sensitive data, a compromised device can bypass all client-side protections.
vulnerabilities.description: No root detection, Play Integrity or SafetyNet attestation was found. For apps handling money or sensitive data, a compromised device can bypass all client-side protections.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use the Play Integrity API (server-verified) and treat client-side root checks as defence in depth.

vulnerabilities.title: Mutable PendingIntent
vulnerabilities.details: PendingIntents are created without FLAG_IMMUTABLE. Apps that receive them (notifications, widgets, other apps) can fill in the base Intent and execute actions with this app's identity/permissions. Only observed inside third-party libraries, which may be unreachable code.
vulnerabilities.description: PendingIntents are created without FLAG_IMMUTABLE. Apps that receive them (notifications, widgets, other apps) can fill in the base Intent and execute actions with this app's identity/permissions. Only observed inside third-party libraries, which may be unreachable code.
vulnerabilities.remediation: Use PendingIntent.FLAG_IMMUTABLE and an explicit target component.

M1.title: Improper Credential Usage
M1.summary: Hardcoded credentials, API keys or tokens shipped in the app, or credentials transmitted/stored insecurely.

M2.title: Inadequate Supply Chain Security
M2.summary: Untrusted third-party SDKs, dynamically loaded code and compromised build or signing pipelines.

M3.title: Insecure Authentication/Authorization
M3.summary: Components and endpoints reachable without proper authentication or authorization checks (exported components, weak custom permissions).

M4.title: Insufficient Input/Output Validation
M4.summary: Untrusted data reaching WebViews, SQL queries, intents or file paths without validation (XSS, SQLi, intent redirection, path traversal).

M5.title: Insecure Communication
M5.summary: Cleartext traffic, disabled certificate validation, trust of user CAs and missing pinning.

M6.title: Inadequate Privacy Controls
M6.summary: Excessive collection of personal data, trackers, device identifiers and leaks through logs, clipboard or screenshots.

M7.title: Insufficient Binary Protections
M7.summary: Missing obfuscation, debuggable builds and absence of tamper/root/debugger detection that make reverse engineering easy.

M8.title: Security Misconfiguration
M8.summary: Insecure manifest defaults: backups, debug flags, task hijacking, permissive file providers and similar configuration issues.

M9.title: Insecure Data Storage
M9.summary: Sensitive data in world-readable files, external storage, unencrypted SharedPreferences/databases or backups.

M10.title: Insufficient Cryptography
M10.summary: Broken algorithms (DES, RC4, MD5, SHA-1), ECB mode, hardcoded keys/IVs and weak randomness.

MASVS-PLATFORM.title: Secure interaction with the platform and other apps

MASVS-CODE.title: Code quality, input validation and dependency hygiene

MASVS-RESILIENCE.title: Resilience against reverse engineering and tampering

malware.label: No malware indicators
malware.note: Heuristic static assessment. A high score means the app is able to behave like malware, not proof that it does. Confirm with dynamic analysis.
